name: ACA §3021/3022
description: Created CMMI (§3021) and MSSP (§3022). Expanded Medicaid and established ACA marketplace plans. Foundation for value-based care architecture.

name: MACRA 2015
description: Repealed SGR. Created QPP (MIPS + Advanced APMs). Sets physician Medicare payment adjustments for most clinicians.

name: Inflation Reduction Act 2022
description: Created Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program. Cycle 1 (10 drugs) live Jan 2026. Cycle 3 underway — first Part B drugs and renegotiations, prices effective 2028.

name: HITECH Act 2009
description: $19B+ for EHR adoption. Created ONC. Foundation for today's health IT infrastructure and eventual API mandates.

name: 21st Century Cures Act 2016
description: Granted ONC interoperability authority. Created FDA RWE Program. Prohibits information blocking. Directly upstream of CMS-0057-F.

name: Medicare Advantage
description: Part C managed care. ~33M enrollees. Funded via risk-adjusted capitation (HCC V28). RADV audits verify coding accuracy. HRRP, VBP penalties do not apply — separate quality bonus system.

name: Medicaid / CHIP
description: State-federal means-tested coverage. Managed care dominates in most states. CMS-0057-F prior auth API mandate applies to Medicaid MCOs. ARP 2021 enhanced federal match still active in many states.

name: QPP / MIPS
description: Quality Payment Program. MIPS scores clinicians 1-100 across four categories; adjusts Part B payment two years later. CMS has proposed sunsetting traditional MIPS beginning the 2029 performance year — accelerating Advanced APM pressure.

name: MSSP / ACO REACH
description: Medicare Shared Savings Program and its evolution ACO REACH. ACOs share savings (or losses) vs spending benchmark. ACO REACH adds health equity adjustments and new benchmark methodology.

name: TEAM Model
description: Transforming Episode Accountability Model. Mandatory bundled payment for surgical episodes (joint replacement, CABG, spinal fusion) in selected regions. Hospitals cannot opt out. Active 2025+.

name: CMS-0057-F
description: Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule. Mandates four FHIR APIs for MA, Medicaid MCOs, and ACA marketplace plans. Jan 2027 compliance deadline. Reduces prior auth turnaround from weeks to days.

name: Drug Price Negotiation
description: IRA Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program. Cycle 1: 10 drugs, Jan 2026 prices, 38-79% discounts. Cycle 2: 15 drugs effective 2027. Cycle 3: negotiating now — first Part B drugs, first renegotiations, prices effective 2028.

name: ESRD / Kidney Care Programs
description: ESRD QIP, Kidney Care Choices (KCC), and Comprehensive Kidney Care Contracting (CKCC). Mandatory ESRD QIP penalizes poor performers. KCC/CKCC are voluntary CMMI value-based models for kidney disease.

name: PAC Quality Reporting
description: Post-Acute Care QRP. Standardized assessment data across SNF (MDS 3.0), IRF (IRF-PAI), and LTCH (LTCH CARE). Required under IMPACT Act 2014. Drives SNF VBP payment adjustments.

name: MA Risk Adjustment (HCC V28 / RADV)
description: HCC V28 transition reduces average MA risk scores — revenue headwind for plans. RADV chart-level audits verify HCC coding accuracy. DOJ scrutiny of upcoding practices intensifying. CMS extrapolation methodology finalized.

name: SCAN Health Plan
description: California-focused Medicare Advantage plan. One of the oldest nonprofit MA plans. Operates primarily in Southern California. Subject to HCC V28 transition and RADV audits.

name: Alignment Health
description: Value-based Medicare Advantage plan with owned provider network. Asset-light + asset-heavy hybrid model. Operates MA plans in CA, TX, NC, AZ. Deep capitation risk with downstream provider partners.

name: Oscar Health
description: Tech-forward health insurer operating ACA marketplace and Medicare Advantage plans. Uses AI for care navigation and prior auth. Heavy FHIR investment. CMS-0057-F compliance infrastructure already being built.

name: Covered California
description: California's ACA marketplace administrator. Coordinates with Medi-Cal (CA Medicaid) on dual-eligible enrollment. Sets plan participation standards and quality requirements for marketplace issuers.

name: Partnership HealthPlan of CA
description: Medi-Cal (California Medicaid) managed care plan covering northern California. Subject to CMS-0057-F Medicaid MCO prior auth API mandate. Coordinates closely with CA DHCS.

name: San Francisco Health Plan
description: San Francisco's Medi-Cal managed care plan. Serves Medi-Cal and Healthy SF members. Subject to CMS-0057-F Medicaid MCO API mandate. Strong community health worker integration.

name: Capital Rx
description: Full-service PBM focused on transparent pricing and drug cost management. Serves health plans including government programs. Positioned as disruptor to legacy PBM model. IRA drug pricing changes affect formulary strategy.

name: Included Health
description: Virtual care and health navigation platform embedded in employer and health plan benefits. Connects members to in-network specialists. Partnered with MA plans for supplemental navigation benefits.

name: Privia Health
description: Physician group management and VBC enablement company. Supports independent physicians participating in MIPS and Advanced APMs. ACO REACH and MSSP participation. National footprint across multiple specialties.

name: Astrana Health
description: Provider-network VBC enablement. Manages ACO REACH-eligible networks and MA capitation risk. California-centered with national expansion. Deep risk-bearing capability at the IPA level.

name: DaVita Kidney Care
description: Largest US dialysis provider. Dominant in ESRD QIP compliance. Participates in CKCC and KCC value-based kidney care models. IRA drug pricing affects Sensipar/Parsabiv which treats ESRD complications.

name: Strive Health
description: Kidney-focused value-based care company. Participates in CKCC Graduated and Global Risk tracks. Works with nephrologists on CKD-to-ESRD transition management. Competes and coordinates with DaVita.

name: Omada Health
description: Digital therapeutics company for diabetes prevention and management, hypertension, and musculoskeletal health. Covered under Medicare Advantage supplemental benefits and employer plans. Outcomes data feeds MIPS quality measures.

name: Hinge Health
description: Digital musculoskeletal (MSK) health company. Covered under MA supplemental benefits and employer contracts. Expanding into surgical decision support (TEAM model adjacent). Outcomes published in peer-reviewed journals.

name: August Health
description: Digital care management platform for skilled nursing facilities (SNFs). Streamlines PAC QRP reporting, PDPM documentation, and care transitions. Directly serves the PAC quality reporting mandate.

name: AdventHealth
description: Large faith-based nonprofit health system (50+ hospitals). Operates in TEAM model-eligible markets. Subject to Hospital VBP, HRRP, and HAC reduction programs. SNF and home health affiliates under PAC QRP.

name: Epic
description: Dominant EHR vendor (~35% of US hospital beds). Must implement CMS-0057-F FHIR APIs. Central to TEFCA exchange. Prior auth API compliance dependent on Epic's implementation roadmap.

name: Redox
description: Healthcare integration platform. Middleware connecting EHRs (including Epic) to digital health apps and payer systems. Key infrastructure for CMS-0057-F API compliance for smaller health systems.

name: Smile Digital Health
description: FHIR server infrastructure company. Powers FHIR implementations for health systems and payers. Core technical layer for CMS-0057-F Patient Access and Provider Directory APIs.

name: Notable
description: AI-powered clinical automation platform. Automates clinical documentation, prior authorization, and patient intake workflows. Positioned to benefit from CMS-0057-F volume shift in prior auth processing.

name: DoseSpot
description: E-prescribing platform. Relevant to OTP (Opioid Treatment Programs) Medicare bundled payment for buprenorphine prescribing. PDMP integration and controlled substance e-prescribing infrastructure.

name: AbbVie
description: Imbruvica (ibrutinib) selected in IRA Cycle 1 drug negotiation — 38% discount from list price. Revenue impact: ~$3B annual Medicare revenue reduction. Accelerating pipeline diversification post-Humira biosimilar competition.

name: Merck
description: Januvia/Janumet selected in IRA Cycle 1. Also has Keytruda (pembrolizumab) expected in future IRA cycles — largest revenue-at-risk drug in Medicare. Major Part B drug target.

name: Amgen
description: Enbrel selected in IRA Cycle 1. Biosimilar competition and IRA negotiation creating dual pressure. Repatha (evolocumab) is a potential future IRA target. Significant Medicare Part D exposure.

name: Roche / Genentech
description: Major Part B drug exposure (Herceptin biosimilar, Avastin, Tecentriq). IRA Cycle 3 includes first Part B drugs — Roche/Genentech directly in scope. FDA RWE submissions for label expansions.

name: GSK
description: Farxiga (dapagliflozin, co-developed) and pipeline drugs face IRA negotiation exposure. Active in respiratory (Breo, Nucala). FDA RWE submissions for post-approval effectiveness evidence.

name: Vertex Pharmaceuticals
description: Trikafta/Kaftrio (elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor) is a potential high-profile future IRA target given its price and Medicare utilization. Also developing CRISPR-based therapies (partnered with CRISPR Therapeutics). Rare disease pricing model under IRA scrutiny.

name: United Therapeutics
description: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (Tyvaso, Orenitram) and rare lung disease drugs. Tyvaso DPI (inhaled treprostinil) is a high-cost Medicare Part D and Part B drug. Future IRA negotiation candidate. Lung transplant innovation via xenotransplantation (eGenesis partnership-adjacent).

name: ConnectiveRx
description: Patient access and affordability programs (copay assistance, prior auth support, hub services). IRA's Part D redesign (out-of-pocket cap) and manufacturer price concession rules directly reshape their copay card programs.

name: Amazon Pharmacy
description: Retail pharmacy disruptor. Partners with MA plans and PBMs for prescription delivery. IRA price transparency and generic drug pricing align with Amazon's low-cost positioning. RxPass subscription for generics.

name: EVERSANA
description: Pharma commercialization and market access company. Manages patient access programs, field reimbursement, and hub services for specialty drugs. IRA price negotiation results restructure their clients' market access strategies.

name: Certara
description: Drug development decision science. Biosimulation, regulatory submissions, and pharmacometric modeling. FDA RWE Program expands the evidence types they help clients generate and submit.

name: Tempus AI
description: AI-driven clinical data platform. Genomic sequencing plus de-identified clinical records. FDA RWE submissions and real-world evidence generation for oncology. Also generates MIPS quality data for oncology practices.

name: Guardant Health
description: Liquid biopsy (circulating tumor DNA). Medicare coverage for SHIELD colorectal cancer screening test. FDA-approved companion diagnostics relevant to IRA negotiation cycle drugs (e.g. Keytruda).

name: GeneDx
description: Genomic testing company specializing in rare disease and pediatric genetics. NIH research partnerships. FDA RWE data source for rare disease drug development. Exome and genome sequencing at scale.

name: RTI International
description: CMS research and evaluation contractor. Runs QPP evaluation, ACO REACH evaluation, and post-acute care research. Direct producer of CMS program performance data. Major government contract holder.

name: Google for Health
description: Google's healthcare division. Health data search, imaging AI (DeepMind AlphaFold/Med-Gemini), and health information infrastructure. EHR integration via FHIR APIs. CMS-0057-F compliance creates expanded API ecosystem Google can access.

name: Coalition for Health AI (CHAI)
description: Multi-stakeholder body (health systems, payers, tech companies, government) developing AI governance frameworks for healthcare. Addresses AI use in prior auth, clinical decision support, and quality measurement — all touched by CMS programs.

name: Anthropic
description: AI safety and applied AI company. Claude models used in clinical documentation, coding assistance, and prior auth automation. Contributes AI safety frameworks referenced by CHAI and ONC health AI guidance.

name: National Institutes of Health
description: Primary federal basic and clinical research funder. NIH-funded research underpins FDA regulatory submissions and IRA drug price justification arguments. All-of-Us program generates RWE-grade real-world health data.

name: CDC
description: Tracks population health metrics used in CMS quality program benchmarking. NHSN (National Healthcare Safety Network) is the source for hospital-acquired infection measures in Hospital VBP and HAC programs.

name: CA Dept of Health Care Services
description: Administers California Medicaid (Medi-Cal) — largest state Medicaid program in US. Contracts with Partnership HealthPlan, SFHP, and other Medi-Cal MCOs. Implements CMS-0057-F Medicaid MCO requirements at state level.

name: CA Dept of Public Health
description: California's public health agency. Coordinates with CDC on population health surveillance. Interacts with health systems and plans on reportable disease, immunization, and public health emergency response.
